sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Amelia.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Mali.
Mali is a country with desert, rivers, music,
and strong traditions in West Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Mali?
Mali is in West Africa.
It is next to Algeria, Mauritania, Senegal, Guinea,
Coteivoir, Burkina Faso, and Niger.
It has no sea, but it has the Niger River,
which is very important for life and farming.
What is the capital city of Mali?
The capital city is Bamako.
Bamako is the largest city in Mali.
It is next to the Niger River.
It has markets, schools, museums, and many motorbikes.
Other cities include Timbuktu,
a famous old city in the desert.
Mopti, a town on the water, Segu and Gao.
How many people live in Mali?
About 22 million people live in Mali.
Most people live in the South, near the river.
Many people live in villages and work in farming
or herding animals.
What language do people speak in Mali?
The official language is French,
but most people speak local African languages,
such as Bambara, the most common.
Songhai, full-fold, Tamashek, spoken by Tuareg people.
What is the weather like in Mali?
Mali is mostly hot and dry.
The north is part of the Sahara Desert.
The south has some rain in summer.
The hot season is from March to June.
The rainy season is from July to September.
The sky is often clear, but there can be dust storms
in the desert.
What does Mali look like?
Mali has the Sahara Desert in the north,
the Niger River in the center,
savannas and fields in the south,
mountains and rock formations in places like Hombori.
It is a land of sand, water and tradition.
What animals live in Mali?
In Mali, you can find camels, donkeys, goats and sheep,
cattle and chickens on farms,
monkeys, foxes and antelopes,
birds, frogs and fish near the river.
Animals are important for food and transport.
What do people eat in Mali?
Malian food is simple filling and made with local crops.
People eat millet, sorghum and rice,
vegetables like onions and okra,
peanuts and beans.
Meat, often goat or chicken when available.
Popular dishes tow a thick porridge made from millet,
rice with peanut sauce,
grilled meat with spicy sauce,
fish stew from the river.
Meals are often eaten together using the right hand.
What do people drink in Mali?
People drink water.
Green tea served in three small glasses.
Milk, especially from cows or goats.
Juice made from hibiscus or bowel bab.
Adults may drink local beer or millet drinks.
Tea is a daily tradition and is shared with friends and guests.
What is life like in Mali?
Life in Mali is often traditional,
family-based and community-focused.
People enjoy working together in the fields,
talking and drinking tea in the shade,
going to the mosque for prayer,
playing music and dancing,
celebrating festivals with colorful clothes.
People wear light cotton clothes,
often in bright colors.
What are some holidays and traditions in Mali?
Independence Day, September 20,
eat alfita and eat al-ada, Muslim holidays.
Traditional music festivals like festival in the desert,
weddings and naming ceremonies.
With food and drums Friday,
the holy day for Muslims.
Mali is famous for its music,
especially the kora, a string instrument.
Some fun facts about Mali.
Timbuktu was once a famous center of learning
and books.
The great mosque of Janae is made of mud
and is very beautiful.
Mali was home to the Mali Empire
and Mansa Musa, the richest man in history.
The flag is green, yellow and red.
Music and storytelling are passed down by griots
or oral historians.
Now you know many things about Mali.
You know where it is,
what people eat,
and how they live.
You learned about the desert, the river,
and the culture.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Bambara.
Ka-kene.
Bye-bye.
